newsitem.title: UGANDA: Uganda says rebels repulsed after border incursion.
newsitem.headline: Uganda says rebels repulsed after border incursion.

text.p: A Ugandan minister said on Sunday that Moslem rebels who invaded from the neighbouring Democratic Republic of the Congo last week were repulsed and driven into the foothills of the Ruwenzori mountain range.
"The army has repulsed the bandits and chased them into the hills. It is now a mopping-up operation," defence minister Amama Mbabazi told reporters in Kampala.

At least forty civilians were killed by the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) rebels, residents fleeing the area said. They said fighting continued on Saturday around the small town of Bundibugyo -- cut off from the rest of Uganda by a spur of the mountains.
The only road connecting Bundibugyo with the rest of Uganda was under attack.

Mbabazi said the rebels did not pose a serious threat. They numbered no more than 300, and he disputed local reports that the ADF rebels had been joined by members of the former Rwandan and Zairean armies.
"There may be one or two of them (Rwandans and Zaireans) but they are totally insignificant," he said.
The Ugandan army commander, Major-General Mugisha Muntu, was directing operations in the Bundibugyo area, Kampala newspapers reported.

Mbabazi said about 700 ADF rebels had been killed since they launched their first attack into western Uganda last November. He said the ADF was a small Moslem fundamentalist group which had been supported by the government of Sudan.
In a press release faxed to Kampala newspapers, the ADF said it had attacked Bundibugyo "to disprove the government's false and wishful allegation that they had stamped us out."
Residents said the rebels looted Bundibugyo after overrunning a small army post on the border last Monday.
The government-owned New Vision newspaper in Kampala reported that over 200 rebels had since been killed in fighting with the Uganda army.

An estimated 12,000 civilians had fled their homes in the area, and there was a serious shortage of food there, the paper added. Uganda's only group of pygmies, now numbering little more than a hundred, lives in the area.
Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni met his top army commanders in Western Uganda last week to discuss operations against the ADF rebels.
